newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: Ethiopia sells 133,765 tonnes of coffee in 96/97.
newsitem.headline: Ethiopia sells 133,765 tonnes of coffee in 96/97.

text.p: Ethiopian coffee authorities on Thursday declared a boom in the industry after exports in 1996/97 (July-June) of a record 133,765 tonnes worth $409.4 million, up from 102,000 tonnes worth $279.5 million in 1995/96.
Abaineh Alemu, deputy general manager of the Ethiopian Coffee and Tea Development Authority, forecast coffee exports in 1997/98 at 128,040 tonnes and earnings at around $348 million.
The 1996/97 exports were well over the 108,000 tonnes forecast by coffee authorities earlier in that year.

Aster Estifanos, head of planning at the development authority, told Reuters in an interview that 119,000 tonnes worth $354.5 million of the total has aready been exported and the balance would be shipped in coming months.
Aster attributed the boom in coffee trade to the government's liberal economic policy, which had created the right environment for all those involved in the industry.
Ethiopia's coffee year is October-September but sales are normally computed on the fiscal year (July-June).

Aster did not give a forecast for exports in 1997/98 but has said Ethiopia wanted to increase production to the 300,000-tonne level, from 200,000 to 250,000 tonnes at present. Ethiopians consume a high percentage of their coffee.

Abaineh said the signs were that the volume of coffee reaching the central market in Addis Ababa and Dire Dawa in the east of the country would rise to 176,220 tonnes in 1997/98 from 165,000 in 1996/97.
Abaineh said the growth in production beyond the 200,000-250,000 tonnes figure was based on development authority plans to help farmers to maximise production.
He said plans to expand the 321,000 hectares of land under coffee were well advanced. He gave no details or figures.
Abaineh said the authority was also in the process of acquiring international certification for its coffee, which is 85 percent organic, to add value to the crop.
Analysts financed by the International Coffee Organization (ICO) are undertaking studies in Ethiopia's coffee growing western region of Welega to produce gourmet coffee, he added.
Ethiopia is Africa's third largest producer of coffee after Uganda and Ivory Coast. Coffee is its main export commodity and accounts for about 60 percent of its foreign exchange revenues.
